pattern_title: Authorization status coding shifts are the largest gating issue
pattern_description: A large share of the increase is tied to authorization status movement rather than a confirmed change in underlying care. The issue recurs across IN, CO, MD, CA, and VA, with the largest impact in IN and additional concentration at RILEY'S CHILDREN'S HEALTH. This should be treated as a gating data and workflow issue before UM, reimbursement, or network actions are taken.

individual_policies.policy_title: Hepatic Fibrosis Testing for Chronic Liver Disease Policy, Professional and Facility - Reimbursement Policy - UnitedHealthcare Commercial and Individual Exchange
individual_policies.evidence: No DRG-specific or authorization-status rule is stated. For the alcoholic hepatitis/cirrhosis clinical area, hepatic fibrosis multianalyte assays 81517 and 81596 are reimbursable only when billed no more than once every six months; listed alternative assays are not separately reimbursable.

individual_policies.policy_title: MEDADV Hepatic Fibrosis Testing Chronic Liver Disease Policy
individual_policies.evidence: This policy is clinically relevant only to liver disease testing within the request. Code 81517 is separately reimbursable when used to distinguish hepatic cirrhosis from non-cirrhosis for listed liver conditions, limited to once every 180 days per member regardless of billing or rendering provider. No authorization rule is stated.

pattern_title: Recurring Medicaid acute hospital pressure is showing up in multiple states
pattern_description: Acute hospital spend is rising across several Medicaid products because admissions are up and, in the largest markets, paid per admit is also higher. CA is the largest driver, but similar patterns repeat in MO, TN, OH, NC, IN, and MD, which makes this a recurring hospital economics and utilization issue rather than a one-off spike. The pattern is concentrated in bowel, liver, and behavioral health-related inpatient DRGs.

pattern_title: Inpatient behavioral health case mix is rising across NC, VA, GA, and UNATTRIBUTED

This is a focused inpatient BH utilization and intensity issue that needs clinical and UM action together.

individual_policies.evidence: This policy is not DRG-specific, but it does apply to inpatient and outpatient facility claims. Drug testing is reimbursable only when medical-necessity criteria are met; in facility settings it is not separately billable and is included in the facility fee. Definitive testing is limited to seven drug classes, proprietary tests are noncovered, and unsupported or routine testing is denied.

pattern_title: CA has a small number of very high-cost Med/Surg outlier cases
pattern_description: CA has a rare-case Med/Surg outlier pattern where a very small number of admissions account for a large share of spend. The biggest driver is anoxic brain damage, with extremely high cost per admit, alongside smaller clusters in alcoholic hepatitis and isolated high-cost bowel surgery cases. This is not a broad utilization trend; it is a case-level severity and payment exposure issue.
